title: Existence of a normalized quotient tensor-completion model
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, and a qcqs scheme X on which l is invertible. There exists a Tensor l E X in the sense of [def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison]: an ordinary tensor model on flat-term K-flat representatives, its normalized quotient-chain augmentation, and a natural isomorphism from its completion to the specified completed tensor, satisfying the representative square. No constructible objects are chosen.

source.place: Coefficient presentation of the projection map; the explicit quotient augmentation is the one of Bhatt--Scholze, Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 6.5.5, as retained in def-sf-projection-tensor-coefficient-comparison

proof.text: Use the explicit ordinary tensor, good-class inclusion and quotient-chain data of def-sf-tensor-quotient-chain-data. The ordinary tensor is the recorded ambient tensor, with its representative comparison restricted from independent-coefficient K-flat complexes to flat-term K-flat complexes.
The constructed quotient chain has tensorOperationUnit as every component. Apply lem-sf-tensor-operation-unit-normalization to obtain both clauses of IsTensorChain.

Apply integralAmbientOperationModels to the identity of X, obtaining its natural tensor-completion isomorphism and the tensor augmentation equation. Transport the shared operation record along ambientPackage_eq; all operations are the recorded constructions. Evaluate on the two good representatives supplied by the first step. The resulting equation is completion unit followed by the comparison and completed-tensor representative isomorphism equals the inverse ordinary representative isomorphism followed by localization of the chain augmentation. Precompose with the ordinary representative isomorphism and cancel its inverse. This proves IsTensorCompletion.

Package the ordinary tensor model, good-class inclusion, natural completion comparison, chain augmentation, and the two established normalization assertions into Tensor. All constructions apply equally to the empty scheme and zero complexes.
